conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: 2026 General Obligation Bond Feasibility, LOBS Alternatives, and School Site Reuse vs. Consolidation
conflicts.summary: DPS operations staff outlined massive long-term capital needs including school consolidations and aging infrastructure, while County staff favored smaller LOBS borrowing over a 2026 GO Bond and County Commissioners pressed for adaptive reuse/teacher housing on surplus sites.
conflicts.side_a_position: Pursue bold capital investment to tackle a $965M+ M&R backlog and address under-enrolled aging elementary schools via consolidation and new construction.
side_a_arguments: DPS faces a $965M+ maintenance and repair backlog and 16 small schools needing long-term capacity solutions.
Board members emphasized failing HVAC systems and 60-to-75-year-old buildings requiring major modernization or consolidation.
conflicts.side_b_position: Prioritize finishing the 2022 bond projects and using incremental LOBS debt rather than a 2026 GO Bond, while exploring UNC DFI adaptive reuse for surplus sites.
side_b_arguments: Roughly $200M of the $460M 2022 bond has been spent so far, raising shovel-readiness questions alongside inflated construction and aluminum costs.

Commissioner Jacobs urged UNC School of Government/DFI partnerships for educator/affordable housing at Old Northern and the DSA campus rather than demolition; Umstead noted UNC SOG feasibility work is already underway.
conflicts.resolution: Informational joint discussion only; both boards deferred further capital and MOU planning to future budget and May joint discussions.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: FY 2026-27 County Tax Capacity vs. DPS Classified Wage Parity and Local Staffing Levels
conflicts.summary: County budget officials argued Durham County is at a fiscal inflection point limiting major new DPS increases without unpopular tax hikes, while DPS Board members defended living-wage parity ($19.22/hr), facility repairs, and local positions amid rising charter pass-through costs.
conflicts.side_a_position: County revenues cannot sustain large annual funding deltas without further property tax increases, requiring scrutiny of DPS local position growth (24%) amid declining ADM (~29,000).
side_a_arguments: County faces only $8.7M in natural revenue growth against $13.5M in baseline expenditure increases before any DPS or county staff raises.
Sales tax growth flattened (+$770K), federal ARPA/SNAP dollars are expiring, and residents have absorbed back-to-back 6% property tax rate increases.
conflicts.side_b_position: Maintain county-matched living wages ($19.22/hr), fix failing school HVAC systems, and recognize that $51M in local funding flows out to charter schools.
side_b_arguments: Board members Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten argued DPS cannot retain classified staff without matching county wage floors and addressing inflation.
DPS has already stabilized its finances, ended lapsed-salary dependency, and absorbed rising charter school tuition shares.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote taken; presentations set the framework for April-June County and DPS budget deliberations.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2026-05-12 9:00 AM - Joint BOCC/BOE Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 12, 2026 Joint BOCC/BOE meeting, members of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and the Durham Public Schools (DPS) Board of Education reviewed Durham Pre-K enrollment and outreach, the County Manager's Recommended Budget, and the DPS FY 2026-27 budget request. Presenters reported 94% enrollment across locally funded non-DPS Pre-K seats, targeted marketing efforts for the Whitted School and wraparound care, and largely flat Pre-K funding (~$500,000 in new county funds after backfilling expiring ARPA dollars). DPS staff outlined priorities for classified employee pay, bus monitor/safety assistant supplements, occupational/physical therapist pay competitiveness, a projected rise in local revenue shared with charter schools from 23% to 26%, $5 million in county capital outlay support, and roughly $13 million in staffing adjustments alongside potential year-end fund sweeps of $3-$4 million. No formal substantive votes or split votes were taken; action on the updated Joint BOCC/BOE Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was deferred without objection to the next joint meeting with the incoming school board before adjournment.

agenda_items.title: Durham Pre-K and Early Education Enrollment, Outreach, and Funding Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented enrollment data across Durham Pre-K's mixed-delivery model (private 5-star childcare providers, Head Start, and DPS classrooms), reporting 94% enrollment in locally funded non-DPS seats against a 96% target, alongside DPS magnet, separate Exceptional Children (266), and braided-funding (541) seats. Presenters highlighted outreach efforts at the Whitted School to counter perceptions that free Pre-K is unavailable and to fill wraparound care, earlier placement timelines, and a county grant-funded universal application portal set to open for the 2027-28 school year. Board members noted that the County Manager's Recommended Budget provides mostly flat funding (~$500,000 in new money after replacing expiring ARPA funds) and discussed strengthening public-private partnerships and exploring K-3 outcome tracking with NCCU and Duke University.

agenda_items.title: County Manager's Recommended Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff, including the County Manager and Keith Lane, provided an overview of the Manager's Recommended Budget presented the previous evening, outlining the fiscal framework and departmental budget constraints. As noted during board discussion, the county asked departments to identify 2% to 3% in cuts to limit the need for a tax rate increase while maintaining core commitments such as $5 million in annual capital outlay support for DPS.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Budget Request, Compensation, and Cost-Savings Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Teeter presented the DPS budget outlook, highlighting board priorities for classified employee pay, bus monitor/safety assistant supplements modeled on prior bus driver supplements, and competitive pay for occupational and physical therapists, while noting DPS is budgeting for charter school revenue sharing to increase from 23% to 26% due to two new charter schools adding 1,000 seats. In response to commissioner questions about internal savings (referencing Commissioner Wendy Jacobs's earlier inquiry), Mr. Teeter described DPS's spring sweep of unused departmental funds (potentially $3-$4 million to reprioritize toward expansion items), zero-based budgeting efforts with Dr. Lewis, and roughly $13 million in staffing reductions tied to enrollment, state funding declines, and charter obligations. Board members also asked about potentially delaying costly programs and the scale of position reductions needed to absorb unfunded increments.

agenda_items.title: Joint BOCC/BOE Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Review and Deferral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee reported that he and DPS Chair Bettina Umstead incorporated submitted feedback into a tightened draft of the Joint BOCC/BOE Memorandum of Understanding and distributed copies for member review. Because the meeting was running an hour behind schedule, Chair Lee proposed deferring formal consideration to the next joint meeting with the newly seated school board, and no board member objected.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham County Board of County Commissioners met jointly on March 11, 2026, approving the meeting agenda and November 19, 2025 joint minutes unanimously. DPS operations leadership presented a sobering draft Capital Improvement Plan highlighting a $965M+ maintenance and repair backlog and potential school consolidations across 16 small schools, while County officials cautioned against a 2026 GO Bond due to unspent 2022 bond balances (~$200M spent of $460M) and rising costs. CFO Jeremy Teter and County Budget Director Keith Lane then clashed constructively over FY 2026-27 finances, with the County warning of an 'inflection point' ($8.7M natural revenue growth against $13.5M baseline county needs after back-to-back 6% property tax hikes) and DPS board members pressing for county-matched $19.22/hr wages and urgent HVAC/facility funding.

agenda_items.title: Welcome, Agenda Review, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the joint quarterly meeting with DPS Board members and Durham County Commissioners and thanked the Multilingual Resource Center interpreters. Both boards unanimously approved the agenda as presented and the November 19, 2025 joint meeting minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (both procedural and minutes motions)

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Planning (CIP) Process and Bond Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS COO Kenneth Barnes and Devon Mitchell outlined a draft CIP addressing a $965M+ maintenance and repair backlog, a 16-school small-enrollment watchlist, potential consolidations (such as Club Blvd and George Watts to the DSA site, Y.E. Smith and Eastway, and Fuller/SDC/Bacon St), and long-range facility needs. County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane stressed shovel-readiness, inflation in aluminum/construction costs, and slower 2022 bond drawdowns (~$200M spent of $460M), signaling reluctance toward a 2026 GO Bond in favor of smaller LOBS increments, while Commissioner Jacobs advocated UNC Development Finance Initiative (DFI) adaptive reuse and teacher housing for Old Northern and DSA.

agenda_items.title: DPS and County FY 2026-27 Budget Presentations and Fiscal Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teter highlighted finance department reforms—two timely audits, ERP modernization, fund balance recovery, ending reliance on lapsed salaries, $51M in charter pass-through costs, and the $19.22/hr living wage model—while County Manager Claudia Hager and Keith Lane warned of an 'inflection point' with only $8.7M in natural revenue growth versus $13.5M in county base pressures, flat sales tax (+$770K), back-to-back 6% tax hikes, ~29,000 DPS ADM, and 24% locally funded DPS staff positions. DPS Board members Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten pushed back on county constraints by emphasizing failing HVAC systems and living-wage parity.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Update Deferral and BOCC-BOE MOU Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to the late hour, both boards gave informal consensus affirmation without a roll call vote to defer the Pre-K update to the top of the May joint meeting agenda and assign representatives to update the outdated BOCC-BOE Memorandum of Understanding before May. Chair Umstead adjourned the meeting at 02:50:49.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus agreement / Adjourned without formal vote

votes.item_title: Approve Joint Meeting Agenda as Presented
ayes: All present members (DPS Board of Education and Durham County Board of County Commissioners)
votes.notes: Joint session of DPS Board of Education and Durham County Board of County Commissioners; BOCC Commissioner Dr. Lee seconded.
votes.discussion_detail: After welcoming attendees and recognizing Multilingual Resource Center interpreters, Chair Bettina Umstead called for a motion to approve the joint quarterly meeting agenda. DPS Board member Natalie Beyer moved approval of the agenda as presented, and Durham County Commissioner Dr. Lee seconded the motion. Neither board requested additions or reordering of items. The motion carried unanimously by voice vote.

ayes: All present members (DPS Board of Education and Durham County Board of County Commissioners)
votes.notes: Joint vote of both governing boards; seconded by BOCC Commissioner Dr. Lee.
votes.discussion_detail: Following approval of the agenda, Chair Bettina Umstead invited a motion on the draft minutes from the November 19, 2025 joint quarterly meeting between the DPS Board of Education and the Durham County Board of County Commissioners. Joy Harrell-Goff moved to approve the November 19, 2025 minutes as presented, and Commissioner Dr. Lee seconded. No edits or corrections were raised by members of either board. The minutes were approved unanimously by voice vote.
